dishes.text: Delicious Smash burger that will wow people and an option fried egg on top

recipe.title: Double Smash Burgers with Onion-Crusted Patties, Burger Sauce & Optional Fried Egg
recipe.description: Twelve paper-thin beef patties smashed onto screaming-hot cast iron until the edges go lacy and mahogany, stacked two-high with melted American cheese, tangy burger sauce, cold crisp lettuce and pickles on a buttered, griddled potato bun — with a runny fried egg on top for anyone who wants one.

ingredients.item: Onions, white, raw — peeled, shaved paper-thin
Tomatoes, raw — cored, cut into 6 mm slices
Iceberg lettuce — outer leaves removed, inner leaves separated (new buy)
Egg (Costco) — for the optional fried egg
Parchment paper, cut into 12 squares about 15 cm (new buy)

steps.title: Ball and chill the raw beef
steps.content: Cut the 1000 g of raw 80/20 ground chuck into 12 pieces of roughly 83 g each. Roll each one into a loose ball with cupped hands — do NOT compress or knead it; the looser the ball, the more lacy and craggy the crust. Set the balls on a plate or tray, cover, and chill in the refrigerator for 20 minutes. Pro tip: cold, loose meat hitting a ripping-hot pan is the entire secret to a smash burger. Do not season them yet — salt on raw meat before smashing draws out moisture and tightens the texture.

steps.title: Mix the burger sauce
steps.content: In a bowl, whisk together 150 g mayonnaise, 60 g ketchup, 30 g yellow mustard, 45 g sweet relish, 1 teaspoon onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon paprika and 1/2 teaspoon garlic salt until smooth and uniformly pale orange. Season with pepper to taste. Cover and refrigerate until assembly — it gets better as it sits.

steps.title: Prep the toppings and the station
steps.content: Peel the white onion and shave 200 g of it paper-thin (a mandoline or your sharpest knife); keep about half in a small bowl for pressing into the patties and half for topping. Core and slice 300 g tomatoes into 6 mm rounds and season them lightly with salt and pepper. Pull off and discard the bruised outer leaves of the iceberg and separate the crisp inner leaves. Drain the 120 g pickle chips well and pat them dry. Cut 12 squares of parchment about 15 cm across. Line everything up next to the stove with the sauce, cheese and a sturdy wide metal spatula — once the beef hits the pan there is no time to go looking for anything.

steps.title: Butter and griddle the buns
steps.content: Split the 6 potato buns and spread the cut faces with about 45 g of the softened butter. Set a large cast-iron or heavy skillet on the stove over medium heat (5-6) and toast the buns cut-side down in batches for 60-90 seconds, until deep golden and glossy at the edges. Stack them on a tray, cut-side up, and set aside. Wipe the pan clean with a paper towel.

steps.title: Preheat the pan hard
steps.content: Return the empty cast-iron skillet (or set a second one alongside it to run two at a time) to the stove over high heat, 9-10, and let it preheat for 10 full minutes until it is faintly smoking. Add 1 tablespoon avocado oil and swirl to a thin film. Turn on your vent hood and open a window — real smash burgers smoke.

steps.title: Smash batch one
steps.content: Place 3-4 cold beef balls in the dry-hot pan with plenty of space between them. Immediately top each with a pinch of the shaved onion, lay a parchment square over the top, and press down hard and straight with the spatula until the patty is about 12 cm across and barely 5 mm thick — commit, 3-4 full seconds of pressure. Peel off the parchment (discard each square after one use), season the tops with salt and pepper to taste, and let them cook undisturbed at heat 8-9 for 90-120 seconds, until the edges are dark brown and lacy and the top has lost its raw red color. Don't crowd the pan — steam is the enemy of crust.

steps.title: Flip, cheese, melt
steps.content: Slide the spatula under each patty at a low angle and scrape hard so the entire brown crust comes up with the meat — the crust is the whole point. Flip, season the second side with salt and pepper to taste, and lay a slice of American cheese on each. Cook 30-45 seconds more, then transfer to a warm tray, stacking them in pairs (two patties, two slices of cheese per burger).

steps.title: Repeat for the remaining batches
steps.content: Wipe the pan with a wadded paper towel between batches to clear burnt bits, add a light film of the remaining avocado oil, let it come back up to near-smoking for about 60 seconds at heat 9, and repeat the smash-season-flip-cheese sequence until all 12 patties are done. Keep the finished stacks loosely covered on the warm tray.

steps.title: Fry the eggs (optional topper)
steps.content: While the last batch cooks, set a nonstick skillet on a second burner over medium-low heat (3-4) and melt about 20 g of the remaining butter. Crack in the 6 raw eggs, season with salt and pepper to taste, and fry gently for 2-3 minutes until the whites are fully set and opaque but the yolks are still liquid. For a slightly firmer top, cover the pan for the last 30 seconds. Slide them out one at a time so the yolks stay intact.

steps.title: Build and serve
steps.content: Spread burger sauce generously on both toasted bun faces. On the bottom bun: pickle chips, then the double patty stack with its melted cheese, then a scatter of the reserved shaved onion, a tomato slice, and a crisp iceberg leaf. For anyone taking the egg, lay the fried egg directly on the hot cheese so the yolk warms through, then crown with the top bun. Press gently, cut in half on the diagonal if you like, and serve immediately — a smash burger waits for no one.

recipe.notes: Protein per serving: about 48 g (about 54 g with the fried egg). Calories per serving: about 960 (about 1050 with the fried egg). New buys: 80/20 ground chuck, potato buns, American cheese slices, mayonnaise, yellow mustard, dill pickle chips, iceberg lettuce, unsalted butter, parchment paper. Make-ahead: the burger sauce holds 5 days refrigerated and is better on day two; onions, tomatoes and lettuce can be cut up to 4 hours ahead and kept covered in the fridge; the beef can be balled and chilled up to 8 hours ahead. Pro tips: freshly ground 80/20 chuck beats pre-packed lean beef by a mile here — ask the butcher counter to grind it coarse for you; run two cast-iron pans side by side so all six burgers land hot at the same time; never press a patty after the flip, that squeezes out the juice you just built; and scrape, don't lift, when you flip. Storage: cooked patties keep 3 days refrigerated — revive them on the Tovala Smart Oven at Steam 250F for 3 minutes, then Broil 1 minute to crisp the crust back up; assemble with fresh buns and toppings.

recipe.title: Twice-Fried Parmesan-Parsley Fries with Garlic Aioli
recipe.description: Shatteringly crisp, golden russet batons fried twice in peanut oil, showered with grated Parmesan and parsley the second they come out of the fat, and served hot next to a glossy, garlicky lemon aioli.

ingredients.item: Russet potatoes, scrubbed, peeled, cut into 1 cm × 1 cm batons
Flat-leaf parsley, leaves only, finely chopped
Egg yolks (whites reserved for another use)
No Sugar Added Ketchup (Sunny Select), for serving

steps.title: Cut and soak the potatoes
steps.content: Peel the 2000 g of russets and square off the sides, then cut them into even 1 cm × 1 cm batons — even thickness is the whole ballgame for fries that finish at the same moment. Drop them into a large bowl of cold water as you go, then let them soak 30 minutes on the counter to rinse off surface starch. Pro tip: a cloudy soaking water is exactly what you want to pour away.

steps.title: Make the raw-yolk garlic aioli
steps.content: While the potatoes soak, put 2 raw egg yolks, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice (squeezed from the lemon), 1 tbsp minced garlic, and a pinch of salt in the blender. Blend on low 10 seconds, then, with the blender running on low, pour in the 240 g avocado oil in a thin, steady stream over about 60–90 seconds until the sauce is thick, pale and glossy. Season with salt and pepper to taste, scrape into a serving bowl, cover and refrigerate until serving. Pro tip: if it ever looks like it's about to break, stop pouring and let it re-emulsify for 5 seconds before continuing.

steps.title: Drain and dry thoroughly
steps.content: Drain the soaked potatoes in a colander, then spread them on clean kitchen towels and pat the batons completely dry, top and bottom. Wet potatoes make hot oil erupt and give you soggy fries — take the extra two minutes here.

steps.title: Heat the oil for the first fry
steps.content: Pour the 2500 g peanut oil into a large heavy pot on the stove, filling it no more than halfway up the sides. Heat over medium-high (about 7 on a 0–10 dial) until the oil reaches 150°C / 300°F, then drop to medium (about 5–6) to hold that temperature. Set a wire rack over a sheet pan next to the stove.

steps.title: First fry — the blanch
steps.content: Fry the potatoes in 4 batches so the oil never drops below about 140°C / 285°F — crowding the pot steams the fries instead of cooking them. Each batch takes 6–7 minutes: the fries should go limp, tender all the way through, and stay pale blonde with no browning. Lift each batch out with a spider and spread it on the wire rack in a single layer.

steps.title: Rest the fries
steps.content: Turn the burner off and let the blanched fries rest on the rack at room temperature for at least 30 minutes (up to 2 hours is fine). This drying-out stage is what builds the glass-like crust on the second fry.

steps.title: Heat the oil for the second fry
steps.content: Bring the same oil back up over medium-high (about 7) to 190°C / 375°F. Have a large mixing bowl and a clean wire rack ready. Grate the 60 g Parmesan and chop the 15 g parsley now so both are ready the second the fries come out.

steps.title: Second fry — the crisp
steps.content: Fry the rested batons again in 4 batches, 3–4 minutes each, until deep golden and audibly crisp when stirred. Let the oil come back up to 190°C / 375°F between batches. Lift each batch straight into the mixing bowl.

steps.title: Season and finish
steps.content: As soon as each batch hits the bowl, hit it with salt and pepper to taste and toss hard — seasoning only sticks while the surface is still glistening. When all four batches are done, toss the whole lot with the grated Parmesan and chopped parsley so the cheese melts into a fine coating.

steps.title: Serve immediately
steps.content: Pile the fries high on a warm platter and serve at once with the cold garlic aioli and 120 g ketchup alongside. Fries wait for no guest — get them to the table within a couple of minutes of the last batch.

recipe.notes: Protein per serving: about 11 g. Calories per serving: about 970. New buys: russet potatoes, peanut oil, Parmesan, flat-leaf parsley, Dijon mustard, 1 lemon. Make-ahead: the first fry and the rest (steps 1–6) can be done up to 3 hours ahead — hold the blanched fries uncovered at room temperature, then do only the 190°C second fry right before serving. The aioli can be made a day ahead and kept covered in the fridge; whisk it once before serving. Pro tips: use a thermometer and let the oil recover to temperature between every batch — that's the single biggest difference between crisp and greasy. Once the oil cools completely, strain it through a fine sieve back into its bottle; it's good for several more frying sessions. Leftover fries revive well in the air fryer, 4–5 minutes at 200°C/400°F in a single layer, shaking halfway.

prepDays.label: Thu, Sep 24 — 2 days before
tasks: Order 80/20 chuck from the butcher counter; ask for a coarse grind, pick up Saturday.
Shop: potato buns, American cheese, mayo, mustard, pickle chips, iceberg, butter, parchment.
Shop: russet potatoes, peanut oil, Parmesan, parsley, Dijon, lemon.
Mix the burger sauce; refrigerate (it's better on day two, holds 5 days).

prepDays.label: Fri, Sep 25 — 1 day before
tasks: Make the aioli; cover and refrigerate.
Check you have a frying thermometer and two cast-iron pans ready.
Clear fridge space for beef, toppings and sauces.

prepDays.label: Sat, Sep 26 — day of
tasks: Morning: pick up the ground chuck.
Up to 8 hrs ahead: ball the beef into 12 portions, separate with parchment, chill.
3 hrs ahead: cut, rinse and blanch the fries (first fry, steps 1–6); hold uncovered at room temp.
4 hrs ahead: slice onions and tomatoes, shred iceberg; cover and refrigerate.
Whisk the aioli; grate Parmesan, chop parsley, cut lemon wedges.
Butter and toast the potato buns; hold warm.
Heat both cast-iron pans screaming hot; heat peanut oil to 190°C.
Second-fry the fries in batches, letting oil recover between each; salt immediately.
Smash the patties, scrape-flip (never press), cheese on, 6 burgers at once.
Fry the eggs last for anyone wanting one on top.
Plate: build burgers with sauce, pickles, lettuce, tomato, onion; fries beside with aioli, Parmesan and parsley.
